The schemabench_0079 database is a collection of tables that store data related to a social networking platform. The tables are organized into several categories, including notifications, activity, friends, groups, messages, profiles, and invitations.
The bp_notifications table stores information about notifications sent to users, including the user who received the notification, the item or activity that triggered the notification, and the date and time the notification was sent. The table also includes a foreign key reference to the wp_users table, which stores information about the users who are members of the social networking platform.
The bp_notifications_meta table stores additional metadata about the notifications, such as the notification type and any additional information that may be relevant to the notification.
The bp_activity table stores information about the activities that users have performed on the social networking platform, such as posting updates, commenting on updates, and joining groups. The table includes information about the user who performed the activity, the activity type, the content of the activity, and the date and time the activity was performed.
The bp_activity_meta table stores additional metadata about the activities, such as the activity type and any additional information that may be relevant to the activity.
The bp_friends table stores information about the friendships between users on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the users who are friends, the date the friendship was established, and any additional information that may be relevant to the friendship.
The bp_groups table stores information about the groups that users have created or joined on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the group name, description, and any additional information that may be relevant to the group.
The bp_groups_members table stores information about the members of the groups on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the user who is a member of the group, the group they are a member of, and any additional information that may be relevant to the membership.
The bp_groups_groupmeta table stores additional metadata about the groups, such as the group name and any additional information that may be relevant to the group.
The bp_messages_messages table stores information about the messages that have been sent between users on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the message sender, recipient, subject, and content.
The bp_messages_recipients table stores information about the recipients of the messages on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the user who is the recipient of the message, the message thread, and any additional information that may be relevant to the recipient.
The bp_messages_notices table stores information about the notices that have been sent to users on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the notice subject, message, and date sent.
The bp_messages_meta table stores additional metadata about the messages, such as the message subject and any additional information that may be relevant to the message.
The bp_xprofile_groups table stores information about the groups of profile fields on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the group name, description, and any additional information that may be relevant to the group.
The bp_xprofile_fields table stores information about the fields that users have created on their profiles on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the field type, name, description, and any additional information that may be relevant to the field.
The bp_xprofile_data table stores information about the data that users have entered into their profiles on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the user who entered the data, the field they entered the data into, and the data itself.
The bp_xprofile_meta table stores additional metadata about the profiles, such as the profile field and any additional information that may be relevant to the field.
The bp_user_blogs table stores information about the blogs that users have created on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the user who created the blog, the blog ID, and any additional information that may be relevant to the blog.
The bp_user_blogs_blogmeta table stores additional metadata about the blogs, such as the blog name and any additional information that may be relevant to the blog.
The bp_invitations table stores information about the invitations that have been sent to users on the social networking platform. The table includes information about the user who sent the invitation, the invitee, the invitation type, and any additional information that may be relevant to the invitation.
The wp_users table stores information about the users who are members of the social networking platform. The table includes information about the user ID and any additional information that may be relevant to the user.
Overall, the schemabench_0079 database is a comprehensive collection of tables that store data related to a social networking platform, including notifications, activity, friends, groups, messages, profiles, and invitations. The tables are organized into several categories and include foreign key references to other tables to ensure data integrity and consistency.

1) Background / Context
BuddyPress is a powerful social networking plugin designed to extend WordPress websites into comprehensive online communities. It is developed and maintained by Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com. BuddyPress provides essential components typical of online social networks, enabling features beyond standard blogging, such as user profiles, activity streams, groups, messaging, and more. 

 2) Objectives
The objective of BuddyPress is to enhance WordPress sites by offering a flexible framework for creating a wide range of community types. It is intended for use in various scenarios, including educational campuses, internal corporate communications, niche interest groups, product-focused communities, and integration with community forums via bbPress.

 3) Stakeholders & Users
- Website Administrators: Responsible for plugin management and configuration.
- End Users: Members of the online community who interact with social features like messaging, groups, and profiles.
- Developers: Those extending or customizing the BuddyPress functionalities for specific needs.

 4) Functional Descriptions
- User Profiles: Allow users to create detailed personal profiles with custom profile fields and visibility settings.
- Account Settings: Enable users to manage personal account settings, including email notifications.
- Groups: Users can create or join groups, forming micro-communities within the site.
- Activity Streams: Facilitate communication through real-time activity streams for members and groups, with sitewide directories.
- Notifications: Deliver smart notifications for various activities and interactions.
- Friendships: Support establishing and managing friendship connections between users.
- Private Messaging: Provide functionality for private conversations between multiple members.

 5) Non-Functional Descriptions
- Scalability: The system should efficiently handle increasing numbers of users as community size grows.
- Integration: Ability to integrate seamlessly with existing WordPress and bbPress installations.
- Usability: Intuitive user interface and navigation to ensure a smooth user experience.
- Security: Ensure secure handling of user data and communications, particularly with messaging features.
- Performance: Maintain responsive loading times and real-time updates for activity streams and notifications.

-- Schema for database: schemabench_0079
CREATE TABLE `wp_users` (
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_info` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`user_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_notifications` (
  `notification_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `item_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `notification_date` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`notification_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_notifications_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_notifications_meta` (
  `meta_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `notification_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `meta_key` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `meta_value` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`meta_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_notifications_meta_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`notification_id`) REFERENCES `bp_notifications` (`notification_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_activity` (
  `activity_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `activity_type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `content` text NOT NULL,
  `activity_date` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`activity_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_activity_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_activity_meta` (
  `meta_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `activity_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `meta_key` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `meta_value` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`meta_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_activity_meta_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`activity_id`) REFERENCES `bp_activity` (`activity_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_friends` (
  `friendship_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id_1` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id_2` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `friendship_date` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`friendship_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_friends_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id_1`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `bp_friends_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id_2`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_groups` (
  `group_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `group_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`group_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_groups_members` (
  `membership_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `group_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`membership_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_groups_members_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `bp_groups_members_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`group_id`) REFERENCES `bp_groups` (`group_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_groups_groupmeta` (
  `meta_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `group_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `meta_key` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `meta_value` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`meta_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_groups_groupmeta_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`group_id`) REFERENCES `bp_groups` (`group_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_messages` (
  `message_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `sender_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `recipient_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `subject` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `content` text NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`message_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_messages_messages_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`sender_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `bp_messages_messages_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`recipient_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_recipients` (
  `recipient_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `message_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`recipient_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_messages_recipients_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`message_id`) REFERENCES `bp_messages_messages` (`message_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_notices` (
  `notice_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `subject` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `message` text NOT NULL,
  `date_sent` datetime NOT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`notice_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_messages_meta` (
  `meta_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `message_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `meta_key` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `meta_value` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`meta_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_messages_meta_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`message_id`) REFERENCES `bp_messages_messages` (`message_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_groups` (
  `group_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `group_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`group_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_fields` (
  `field_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `field_type` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `field_name` varchar(255) NOT NULL,
  `description` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`field_id`)
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_data` (
  `data_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `field_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `data_value` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`data_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_xprofile_data_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `bp_xprofile_data_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`field_id`) REFERENCES `bp_xprofile_fields` (`field_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_xprofile_meta` (
  `meta_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `field_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `meta_key` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `meta_value` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`meta_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_xprofile_meta_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`field_id`) REFERENCES `bp_xprofile_fields` (`field_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_user_blogs` (
  `blog_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `user_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `blog_info` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`blog_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_user_blogs_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`user_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_user_blogs_blogmeta` (
  `meta_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `blog_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `meta_key` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `meta_value` text DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`meta_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_user_blogs_blogmeta_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`blog_id`) REFERENCES `bp_user_blogs` (`blog_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;

CREATE TABLE `bp_invitations` (
  `invitation_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `sender_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `invitee_id` int(11) NOT NULL,
  `invitation_type` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`invitation_id`),
  CONSTRAINT `bp_invitations_ibfk_1` FOREIGN KEY (`sender_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT `bp_invitations_ibfk_2` FOREIGN KEY (`invitee_id`) REFERENCES `wp_users` (`user_id`) ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb3;
